Subject: Solace-13B intake: tokenizer parity, fallback variants, and staged pin

Team —

Solace Labs shared the v1 release of Solace-13B yesterday; Samir is on cc for any artifact questions. From an intake perspective we ran a quick eval on our staging cluster and found two items I want to surface before we proceed with the standard onboarding flow:

- Tokenizer parity: some of our test prompts show token counts +1/+2 compared to our baseline tokenizer, which affects billing and batching heuristics. Samir — can you confirm which tokenizer configs were used (byte-level, pre-tokenization tweaks)?
- Fallback variants: Solace provided a 7B distilled variant and a 13B quantized variant. We need a clear compatibility matrix for fallbacks (same vocab, KV-cache format) so the runtime can safely route.

Proposal: provisional staged pin for Solace-13B on a small subset of capacity (staging pool) for 7 days while we complete tokenizer parity and ABI checks. If checks pass, expand to wider preprod and schedule a canary rollout.

Attachments: I attached the raw compat logs and a short staged-pin proposal.

Ask: Karthik — can infra run the tokenizer parity job (full prompt set) and confirm KV-cache binary compatibility? Laura — product needs a short note on expected latency delta vs our baseline so we can set SLA expectations for the Dedicated customers. Marissa — can you hold on routing policy changes until we confirm fallback safety?

Thanks —
Olga
Principal Product Manager, Model Onboarding
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Solace-13B intake: tokenizer parity, fallback variants, and staged pin

Thanks Olga — starting the tokenizer parity runs now. Quick notes from an infra perspective:

1) Tokenizer: early flag is this looks like a normalization/whitespace pre-tokenization mismatch (we see 1–2 extra tokens around long-form bullets). I'll run the full prompt set this afternoon and push results to the Drive link.
2) KV-cache / ABI: Solace claims the same KV layout but uses little-endian byte ordering in their serialized cache for the quantized variant. Our runtime expects network-order big-endian for cross-variant resume/caching. That will break automatic fallback unless we add a shim or force re-encoding on ingest.

Requesting clarification from Samir: is the little-endian artifact by design for your quantized pipeline? If so, we either need a binary compatibility shim (adds ~3–5ms at resume) or to block fallback until we roll a conversion step into the admission pipeline.

I attached a short parser dump and an early incompatibility example.

- Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer

Hi all —

Thanks for the quick look. A couple clarifications:

- Tokenizer: we used a tweaked BPE tokenizer with a pre-normalization pass (NFKC) to align with some downstream training pipelines. The config and vocab are in the artifacts link: https://s3.solacelabs.ai/artifacts/solace13b/tokenizer.tar.gz. If NFKC is the mismatch, it should be straightforward to provide a compatibility mapping or a tokenizer build that mirrors your NFKC-less pipeline.
- KV-cache endian: the quantized export tool we use writes little-endian by default on x86; that was not intended to be a breaking change. We can re-export big-endian or provide a conversion routine.

If it helps, we can produce a converted kv-cache bundle for the quant variant and a tokenizer build with NFKC disabled for your ingestion tests by EOD tomorrow.

Samir

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the offer Samir. Given the KV endian mismatch and the tokenizer NFKC divergence, here's my recommended path forward so we don't hold the intake pipeline up longer than necessary:

1) Staged pin (7 days) on staging pool only. No traffic from production customers, but run the full prompt set (Karthik) + latency microbench (Laura).
2) Solace to provide: an NFKC-free tokenizer bundle and a converted big-endian KV-cache for the quant variant (Samir said EOD tomorrow).
3) Infra to implement a temporary ingest conversion shim for the quant variant only if Solace cannot deliver big-endian exports by the end of the staged pin. We accept the 3–5ms resume overhead for staging validation but will not allow that shim in production without a perf SLA.
4) Product to draft a short note on SLA delta and fallback policy for the console UI; ops/SDR messaging will be blocked until we confirm final behavior.

Please reply with quick +1 or concerns so I can lock the staged pin this morning and open JIRA-INTAKE-4123 for tracking.

Olga
